title: Aureline M5 structured-versus-heuristic fallback evidence drill set
description: Canonical, export-safe object model that freezes the structured-native versus heuristic-fallback proof corpus: one parse-evidence case — a native structured diagnostic, a normalized task event, an imported provider annotation, or a heuristic text parse — exercised through a failure drill (native baseline, malformed output, stale run, superseded retry, reconnect, lost channel, partial export, imported evidence, or output-channel virtualization) and rendered onto the claimed M5 tooling profiles (Problems panel, output channel, terminal runner, debug console, notebook output, pipeline overlay, AI-tool evidence, support export). Each case carries enough identity to re-derive an effective claim without trusting a grade: a heuristic fallback reads visibly distinct from native/structured evidence on every profile and keeps a raw-output backlink; the problem-source class, run/step/provider/channel lineage, and stable channel id stay reopenable on demand on every profile; a reconnect or lost-channel drill never drops evidence, a partial export stays reviewable without the originating UI, and an imported/remote/pipeline origin never claims live local authority; stale, superseded, and missing freshness and stale/missing verification proofs narrow a first-party case rather than reading as fresh; an output-channel virtualization drill that loses stream-first paging, search, or copy/export narrows; a profile that renders wider than the case's effective claim floors as an overclaim; and a case that flattens its source class, lets a heuristic read as structured, flattens lineage, diverges its canonical ids, drops a heuristic backlink, loses its reopen path, drops evidence on reconnect, exports a non-self-contained slice, lets a profile overclaim, or lets an imported origin claim live floors to a raw-output / keyboard fallback rather than rendering a clean-but-false row. This is the proof-corpus companion to schemas/tooling/m5-execution-evidence.schema.json (the lane matrix), schemas/tooling/m5-problem-records.schema.json (the Problems row), schemas/tooling/m5-execution-evidence-projections.schema.json (the projected overlay), schemas/tooling/m5-chronology-reuse.schema.json (the chronology entry), and schemas/tooling/m5-output-channels.schema.json (the output channel); all share one vocabulary so Problems, output-channel, terminal, debug, notebook, pipeline, AI-tool, and support surfaces ingest one model. Adding an enum value is additive-minor and requires a schema_version bump; repurposing an existing value is breaking and requires a new decision row.

redaction_class_token.description: Default redaction posture for the packet. No raw stdout/stderr bytes, command lines, provider log bodies, env bodies, absolute paths, URLs, or secrets ever cross this boundary; refs carry opaque ids only.

problem_source_kind.description: The problem-source class — the structured-versus-heuristic axis. A heuristic_output_parse case (or a heuristic confidence tier) must read visibly distinct from structured evidence and keep a raw-output backlink.

output_channel_class.description: Output-channel / evidence class. A real channel (anything but not_applicable) must carry a stable canonical channel id.

drill_kind.description: The failure drill a parse-evidence case is exercised through (the scenario axis, orthogonal to the problem-source axis).

tooling_profile.description: A claimed M5 tooling profile a case is rendered onto. ai_tool_evidence and support_export are exported packets that must stay self-contained.

claim_posture.description: Whether the case is publicly claimed. Labs/unadvertised cases make no public claim and are never widened.

origin_class.description: How the run/evidence originated. First-party origins certify; remote, pipeline/provider, and imported origins render as read-only overlays only.

confidence_tier.description: Confidence taxonomy shared with the causality matrix. A heuristic tier marks a heuristic case that must read distinctly and keep a raw-output backlink; unmapped is a first-class state, not an invisible gap.

freshness_state.description: Freshness state of the evidence. Stale and superseded states must remain visibly classified wherever the case is rendered.

reopen_target.description: Where reopen-to-origin lands. A floored case keeps a raw_output_backlink or none_keyboard_fallback rather than rendering a clean-but-false row.

proof_currency.description: Currency of the certification proof that this case preserves its causal chain (distinct from the evidence's own freshness_state).

fallback_claim.description: The effective claim a case or a rendering profile asserts. A profile may never render wider than the case's effective claim.
